t: The god watched over that birth. I am certain of it.
A safe child is a blessing. We should give thanks.
The god kept both of them here. That matters.
Maybe the god helped. I am mostly glad they are safe.
A birth like that makes belief easier for a day.
I do not know who deserves thanks. I will thank everyone.
Good hands delivered that child. Do not forget the people in the room.
Births go well sometimes. That does not make them miracles.
I am glad they lived. I will leave the god out of it.
The god made the ground generous. We should not waste what grew.
That harvest has the god's hand all over it.
The land answered because the god willed it. Give thanks.
It could be a blessing. It could be a very good season.
I want to call that providence. I am not quite there.
Whatever caused it, we should fill the stores while we can.
Good soil and good weather can surprise people. That is enough explanation.
The fields had a strong year. Fields do that.
Call it a miracle after the next harvest does the same.
The god threw them down. There is no softer way to say it.
That landing was judgment. I would mind where I stand.
The god spared them the worst of that fall.
Something put them on the ground. I cannot say what.
I believe the fall. The reason for it is harder.
That sounds like power. Whether it was divine power, I do not know.
A bad fall becomes a miracle once enough people repeat it.
They hit the ground hard. That part needs no god.
Show me where they landed before you tell me what caused it.
The god lifted them for everyone to see. That was no accident.
Being raised like that marks a person. We should pay attention.
The god took hold of them and set doubt aside.
I believe they rose. I still do not know why.
That is hard to explain without the god. Hard is not impossible.
If you truly saw their feet leave the ground, I need time.
People jump, stumble, and remember badly. I need more than one account.
Nobody floats. That tells me the story grew somewhere.
I would need to see that with my own eyes.
The god saw the wolf and saw who suffered. Help will come.
We should pray for them and sharpen every spear.
The god spared their life. We must tend the wounds.
Maybe someone watched over them. The wounds are real either way.
I do not know why the god allowed it. I am glad they survived.
That makes me want a prayer and a stronger fence.
Wolves bite people when we let them close. Build the fence.
There is no message in teeth. There is only a hungry wolf.
Praying later will not help as much as carrying a spear now.
The god made the broken thing whole. That is mercy.
No tool did that work. Give the god the credit.
The god restored what we could not. We should remember it.
It was broken, and now it is not. I cannot explain the middle.
That sounds like a miracle. I am surprised to hear myself say it.
Maybe the god repaired it. Someone should still inspect the work.
Someone fixed it and failed to mention it. That happens.
Repairs look impossible when nobody sees the worker.
I want to see the break before I believe it vanished.
The god received them. We should care for the people left behind.
Their life mattered to the god. It should matter to us.
We will pray for the dead and bring food to the family.
I hope someone was there at the end. I hope the god was.
Death makes me want to believe and doubt at the same time.
I do not know where they went. I know who will miss them.
They died. We should speak about their life, not invent an answer.
Death is hard enough without pretending we know what follows.
Help the family in front of us. Leave the next world alone.
The god fed us when the stores failed. We owe thanks.
Food appearing when we needed it is providence made plain.
The god heard an empty stomach and answered it.
Maybe the food was given. Maybe somebody left it. We should still share it.
I want that to be an answer. Hunger makes belief tempting.
The timing is difficult to dismiss. I am still trying.
Food has owners, even when nobody saw them arrive.
Count the baskets twice before calling supper a miracle.
Someone carried that food. We should find them and say thanks.
The god shook the ground beneath us. That was a warning.
Even the earth moves when the god commands it.
We should check every wall and then give thanks for surviving.
The earth moved, certainly. Whether the god moved it is another question.
That shaking felt deliberate. I do not like what that suggests.
I nearly prayed while it happened. I am still deciding what that means.
Ground shifts. It does not need hands to move.
Check the foundations before everyone starts preaching about the shaking.
Fear makes patterns quickly. An earthquake is frightening enough by itself.
The god put them down gently. Mercy followed power.
They were returned safely because the god chose it.
Give thanks that the god set them down instead of dropping them.
A gentle landing does make the story harder to dismiss.
Something lowered them. I cannot decide whether that comforts me.
I believe they came down safely. I am unsure about the rest.
People land on their feet sometimes. That is not divine proof.
The gentle part sounds added afterward. Stories like tidy endings.
Show me where it happened. I want more than a careful retelling.
The god struck them. We should ask what brought that judgment.
Lightning from a clear sky is no ordinary death.
The god answered with wrath. Nobody should celebrate that lightly.
That sounds like the god, and I wish it did not.
If it was judgment, I want to know what was judged.
A clear sky makes chance harder to believe. Not impossible, just harder.
Lightning is lightning. Clear skies do not make it a sentence.
People call every strange death judgment after the person cannot answer back.
I believe they were struck. I do not believe anyone chose it.
The god cast them aside. That kind of power deserves caution.
Nobody flies that far without the god's hand behind it.
The god threw them and still let them live. Remember both parts.
I believe something threw them. Naming it is where I hesitate.
That story frightens me more if the god truly did it.
People do not move like that. I admit the obvious explanation is difficult.
A tumble looks like a flight when the witness is frightened.
I need distance, marks, and another witness before I believe that throw.
The story traveled farther than the person did. I would wager on that.
The god pulled that tree from the earth. Nothing else could.
Roots and all means the god wanted our attention.
The god cleared the ground with one act. We should ask why.
A whole tree coming up is difficult to explain. I will grant you that.
Maybe the god moved it. Maybe the roots were already gone.
I would like to see the hole before I decide what happened.
Rot takes roots before anyone sees it. Then one hard pull finishes the work.
Trees fall strangely on bad ground. That is not a sermon.
Show me sound roots and no tools. Then I will listen.
